metaDesc: A tight, realistic 7-day Thailand itinerary: 2 days in Bangkok, 2 in Chiang Mai, and 3 on a Krabi Andaman island — day-by-day plans, travel times, costs and where to stay. Two short flights, no wasted days.
keywords: thailand 7 day itinerary, one week in thailand, thailand itinerary 7 days, bangkok chiang mai krabi week, thailand week route, thailand short trip plan
ogDesc: City, mountains and islands in one week: 2 days Bangkok, 2 Chiang Mai, 3 on the Krabi islands. Day-by-day plan, travel times, costs and where to stay — the fast version of the classic route.
intro: One week is enough to taste the three sides of Thailand — the buzz of Bangkok, the culture and cool air of Chiang Mai, and the limestone islands of the Andaman coast. It moves faster than the classic 10-day trip, so you keep the highlights and cut the slow days. This is the efficient week, day by day, with travel times, rough costs and where to stay.
quickAnswerHtml: The best 7-day Thailand itinerary for first-timers is Bangkok → Chiang Mai → Krabi: 2 days in Bangkok (temples, markets, street food), 2 in Chiang Mai (old-town temples, an ethical elephant sanctuary), then 3 on the Krabi islands (Railay, island-hopping). Connect the legs with two short domestic flights booked in advance.
quickAnswerH2: The perfect week in Thailand, in one line

blocks.html: The short version: fly into Bangkok, give it 2 focused days, then take a 1-hour domestic flight to Chiang Mai for 2 days of temples, mountains and slow mornings. Fly south to Krabi for 3 days of beaches and island-hopping, and fly home from Krabi (or hop to Phuket). Two short flights tie it together — book them early and they're cheap. Wondering what you give up versus a longer trip? See what a week trades off below.

blocks.html: Start where almost everyone lands. With only two days, be deliberate: grand temples in the cool of the morning, street food at night. Base yourself right on the BTS/MRT (Sukhumvit or Silom) so you're never stuck in traffic — this matters more when your time is short.

items: Day 1: the big hitters early — Grand Palace, Wat Pho's reclining Buddha, Wat Arun across the river; then Chinatown (Yaowarat) for street food after dark. See the Grand Palace & temples guide and skip-the-line tickets on the Bangkok attractions & tickets page
Day 2: a market morning (Chatuchak on weekends, or a floating/train market), a food tour, and a rooftop bar at sunset — then pack, because you fly north tomorrow

The one thing to skip on a 7-day trip

blocks.html: On the 10-day route we add an Ayutthaya day trip and a third, slower day in each city. In a week, those are the first things to cut — a day trip out of Bangkok eats a whole travel day you don't have. If ruins are a must-see for you, take a half-day tour instead, or save it for a longer visit. Not sure a week is enough? Compare the 10-day itinerary and the 2-week itinerary.

A one-hour flight lands you in a completely different Thailand: cooler air, a moated old town, hundreds of temples and mountains on the doorstep. Two days here is tight but works if you keep the old town and one big experience. See how to get from Bangkok to Chiang Mai (flight vs sleeper train).

items: Day 3: wander the old-town temples on foot (Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh), then sunset at Doi Suthep above the city and the night bazaar after. Tickets and tours on the Chiang Mai attractions page

Day 4: pick your one big morning — an ethical elephant sanctuary (choose no-riding, observation-first camps) or a Thai cooking class. With more time you'd do both; with a week, choose the one you'll remember

blocks.title: Where to stay in Chiang Mai
blocks.text: The old town puts you walking distance from the temples, markets and cafés — ideal when you only have two days.

blocks.html: Finish on the Andaman coast, where the limestone cliffs drop straight into turquoise water. Fly Chiang Mai → Krabi (usually via a quick Bangkok connection) and base in Ao Nang or Railay. Three days is the right amount to arrive, hop the islands and still get one slow beach day. See the Krabi tours & tickets and our island-hopping guide.

items: Day 5: arrive, settle into Ao Nang or take the longtail to car-free Railay for cliffs and calm beaches
Day 6: the classic island-hopping day — Phi Phi, the Hong Islands or the 4-Islands tour by speedboat
Day 7: one slow morning on a quiet beach, then fly home from Krabi — or ferry over to Phuket if you're flying out of there. Deciding between the two coasts? Read Phuket vs Krabi

blocks.title: Where to stay in Krabi
blocks.text: Ao Nang for restaurants and ferry access; Railay for cliffs and quiet.

blocks.text: What a week trades off (and how to reshape it)

blocks.html: Seven days keeps every highlight but leaves less slack. You skip the Ayutthaya day trip, get one big experience per city instead of two, and land one island stretch rather than two. Here's how to bend the route to your taste.

blocks.caption: How to adapt the efficient week

Bangkok (3) → Chiang Mai (3), sleeper train south skipped
Bangkok (1) → Krabi + Phi Phi or Koh Lanta (5–6)
Add a slow day per city + an Ayutthaya trip

blocks.title: Know before you go (for this route)

items.title: Book the two domestic flights early
items.text: Bangkok–Chiang Mai and Chiang Mai/Bangkok–Krabi are cheap booked weeks ahead and pricey last-minute. On a tight week, pick morning flights so you don't lose a half-day in the air.

items.title: Pack carry-on only
items.text: With two flights in seven days, checked bags cost extra on the budget airlines and slow you down at every airport. A carry-on keeps the whole trip moving.

items.title: Best months are Nov–Mar
items.text: Cool, dry season is ideal countrywide. Songkran (mid-April) is peak heat but a once-in-a-lifetime water festival. See best time to visit below.

items.title: Andaman vs Gulf in wet season
items.text: If you travel May–Oct, the Gulf islands (Samui, Phangan) often stay drier than Krabi. Flip the beach leg accordingly — but note the Gulf adds a longer transfer.

faq.a: Yes — a week is enough to see three contrasting sides (Bangkok, Chiang Mai and one island stretch) if you connect the legs with short domestic flights and skip slower add-ons like day trips. You'll move faster than a 10-day trip, but you won't feel rushed if you base yourself smartly and book flights in advance.

faq.q: What is the best 7-day Thailand route for first-timers?
faq.a: Bangkok (2 days) → Chiang Mai (2 days) → Krabi or the islands (3 days). It gives you city, culture and beaches in one loop, and the two internal flights are short and inexpensive when booked ahead. Fly home from Krabi to avoid backtracking.

faq.q: How much does a 7-day Thailand trip cost?
faq.a: Excluding international flights, budget travellers can do a week on roughly US$40–60 a day, mid-range around US$80–150 a day, and comfortably more at the top end. Domestic flights, island tours and nicer hotels are the main variables. See our Thailand daily budget guide for a full breakdown.

faq.q: Should I add a fourth stop in one week?
faq.a: It's better not to. With only seven days, a fourth base means another travel day and less time actually enjoying each place. Keep it to three stops — Bangkok, Chiang Mai and one island region — and save extra destinations for the 10-day or 2-week version of this route.

faq.q: When is the best time to do this itinerary?
faq.a: November to March (cool, dry season) is best across all three regions. April is very hot but includes Songkran. In the May–October wet season, favour the Gulf islands (Koh Samui, Koh Phangan) over the Andaman coast for drier weather.
